## Runtime correctness clarification

### CR-004a Unambiguous structural fields
Compiler format 2 SHALL distinguish null (`null:`) from every non-null field. A non-null field SHALL encode its invariant-decimal UTF-16 code-unit length, `:`, and four uppercase hexadecimal digits for every code unit. This preserves punctuation, empty strings, supplementary pairs and accepted unpaired surrogates without UTF-8 replacement aliases. Numeric formatting SHALL be invariant; schema identities SHALL be sorted ordinally while authored ordering remains intact. Absent, literal named and opaque-selector outcomes SHALL remain distinct. Compiler format and the other existing binding/acceptance exclusions remain outside fingerprint inputs; fixed codec format remains included. Opaque code changes still require a new authored version. This completes unreleased format 2 and promises no legacy alias.

## Runtime correctness clarification

### DU-013a Position facts fence checkpoint changes
Every committed execution-envelope change SHALL advance the optimistic workflow stream version. Yield and fiber failure SHALL append `WorkflowExecutionPositionChangedEvent` atomically with their checkpoint, even without another fact. Providers SHALL round-trip the new discriminator with all inherited workflow-event fields and preserve checkpoint parent/root lineage through replacement and null clearing. The original 21 workflow mappings and their bytes and the separate DAG framing remain unchanged. The twenty-second workflow mapping is additive; matched protocol/provider binaries and fresh/reset stores are the qualification target. No mixed-version rollout or applied-migration compatibility is implied. See DR-012a and the exact advanced declaration in document 17.

## Runtime correctness provider qualification

### PR-024a Position-fact and checkpoint-lineage certification
Every retained durable provider SHALL certify the additive workflow position event, atomic expected-version fencing of position-only yield and fiber-failure commits, and checkpoint parent/root lineage on insert, replacement and clearing. Tests SHALL use two independently constructed stores/runtimes against the same database/schema for checkpoint/tail and post-tail publication races. Full provider suites supplement these cases; a single store object or in-memory success alone is insufficient evidence. PostgreSQL qualification includes the reviewed lineage columns/read/upsert change. SQL Server correctness does not qualify its whole-document/history scaling or change the separately selected support scope. Fresh-store tests do not certify migration of an already-journaled initial schema.

## Runtime concurrency and identity acceptance (AC-322–327)

- **AC-322** *Position-only fencing* — **[provider, advanced]** Two independently constructed stores sharing one database/schema reject the stale host after yield and fiber-failure checkpoint commits; the winning position and lineage survive. [DU-013a, PR-024a]
- **AC-323** *Coherent publication* — **[provider, advanced]** Deterministic competing-host commits between checkpoint/tail reads and after tail capture produce one logical outbound event, with no stale checkpoint publication. [DR-012a]
- **AC-324** *Integrity quarantine* — Identical unreconciled positions quarantine with an offending-event diagnostic; a conflicted park reloads; cancellation remains authoritative; rearm without repair parks again while preserving checkpoint and bad tail. [DR-012a]
- **AC-325** *Absolute deadline election* — Controlled-clock root/branch/item cases cover before/at/after deadline, early/delayed timers, wrapper failure and election-to-notification delay. An elected winner remains stable and losing work keeps physical ownership until settlement. [CR-018]
- **AC-326** *Structural identity* — Both workflow modes distinguish field punctuation, null/absent/named outcomes and accepted Unicode code units; cultures cannot change schema ordering. Normalized equivalent host profiles are idempotent and all behavior-affecting conflicts reject before service mutation. [CR-004a, PR-040]
- **AC-327** *Measured qualification boundaries* — Long-loop evidence at small/default command budgets counts added facts, serialized bytes and commit boundaries. Evidence records the exact source, compiled scope and actual results without claiming untested migration, mixed-version, process-crash or storage-scale guarantees. [DU-013a, PR-024a]

## Runtime correctness clarification

### DR-012a One captured checkpoint and a fully classified tail
The loader SHALL return the same captured checkpoint used to reconstruct the aggregate, with its ordered complete tail read from that version. The driver SHALL NOT advance an expected version while retaining an unreconciled position. Any position-changing fact that cannot be reconstructed from the captured envelope SHALL cause a full reload. Terminal/cancellation/park/retry state governs execution; every tail event must be classified. Changing contention has bounded retries and retains its continuation retry path.

Consecutive identical checkpoint bytes/version and ordered immutable event identities at the same stream version, when still unreconciled, SHALL quarantine with the offending event type. A concurrent append that rejects the park SHALL cause reload. Quarantine writes no replacement checkpoint, and rearming unchanged bad state SHALL park again. The diagnostic SHALL state that no supported checkpoint repair exists and that an engine or provider defect is indicated. No public repair/rearm API is admitted.

Current providers purge whole instances atomically; no supported retention trims a tail needed after a retained checkpoint. The ordered complete append-only provider guarantee is sufficient here. Counting tail objects is not sequence validation. A partial-history or weaker-consistency feature must revisit this guarantee before admission.

## Workflow position-fact protocol addition

The advanced `OrcaCore.Runtime.Protocol` assembly admits this exact additional declaration:

```csharp
namespace OrcaCore.Abstractions.Durable;
public sealed record WorkflowExecutionPositionChangedEvent : WorkflowEvent;
```

It adds no payload members beyond inherited `WorkflowEvent` identity, instance, command, causation, occurrence-time and optional `ParentInstanceId`/`RootInstanceId` lineage fields. The fixed codec discriminator is `WorkflowExecutionPositionChangedEvent`, the twenty-second workflow mapping. The prior 21 workflow mappings and `orcacore-json-v1` bytes and the separate DAG framing remain unchanged. Yield/fiber-failure checkpoint commits include this fact as an optimistic concurrency fence; the fact does not contain or reconstruct the replacement envelope. Providers use the existing atomic expected-version append contract. This is an advanced provider/custom-host record, not an application authoring node or public repair operation. Matched binaries and fresh/reset stores are required for this greenfield addition.
